subject: Dedicated capacity sizing for HelioSync — surge headroom & SLO alignment

Cc: procurement@heliosync.ai

Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing for HelioSync — surge headroom & SLO alignment

Jordan / Samir —

Thanks again for the deep dive yesterday. I promised to follow up with a concise operational proposal that ties the 2-week pilot profile you shared to a Dedicated capacity recommendation and a practical surge hedge. High-level summary first, details below and attached model: heliosync_commit_model_v1.xlsx.

Ask: can you confirm the pilot average token size (~150 tokens per request) and whether the majority of traffic will be short multi-turn chat (2–4 turns) versus long single-shot prompts? That drives our KV-cache assumptions.

Quick recommendation (emergency- and production-ready):
- Baseline reserved slab: 12 x A100 (80GB) equivalent GPUs for sustained steady-state to meet 200k tokens/sec aggregated across your endpoints at p50 generation latencies ~95ms.
- Burst buffer: additional 6 x A100-equivalent on a burst pool for spikes up to 420k tokens/sec (2.1x baseline) for up to 30-minute windows.
- Latency SLO fit: target p95 <= 350ms for the primary model (1.8B dense variant) with the above configuration and a mix of batching (40–100ms batching window) + prefix KV caching.
- Headroom: ~2.1x token/sec headroom in burst pool; operational fallback to a quantized 4-bit variant with slightly lower quality if GPU pool saturates.

Why this split? Your traffic traces show a 95th percentile of short spikes that last ~15–20 minutes. A 12+6 split keeps committed costs predictable while letting you absorb short surges without SLAs failing. We sized the baseline to match steady throughput assuming 60% cache hit (multi-turn reuse). If cache hit is lower (<=30%), we should move to 16 baseline GPUs or increase cache warming policies.

Attachments: the workbook includes token/sec simulations under three cache-hit scenarios, per-model latency curves, and a conservative billing estimate. Also included a short playbook (redwood_capacity_playbook.pdf) with runbook steps for cache warmup and automatic fallback.

Next steps: please review and confirm the 150-token assumption and whether p95 350ms is acceptable. If yes, I’ll loop in Kimberly + Priyom to finalize slab SKU mapping (A100 vs H100) and draft the Dedicated contract amendment.

Thanks —
Ethan

Thanks Ethan — this is helpful and aligned with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- Confirmed: median request ~140–160 tokens; 70% of requests are short multi-turn conversational flows (2–3 turns); 30% are single long prompts (300–800 tokens).
- p95 target: our product team wants p95 <= 300ms for primary workspace endpoints (users notice anything above ~350ms). For background batch endpoints the p95 can be relaxed to 700ms.

Two asks:
1) Can you show an alternate mapping that uses an H100-heavy slab (H100 80GB) for lower p95 at the same token/sec?
2) What does the fallback quality delta look like if we switch to INT4/4-bit quantized variants under burst? We need to communicate quality impact to the product team.

Samir: looping you in for procurement timing.

Ethan / Kim / Marissa —

Quick sanity check and proposed H100 alternative attached (see updated workbook tab "H100-mapping"). Short summary:

1) Token/sec baseline assumptions used:
- 1 x A100 (80GB) equivalent can sustain ~16k tokens/sec for the 1.8B dense model with 60% KV hit and 40ms end-to-end batching amortization (p50 ~85ms, p95 ~310ms for short requests).
- 1 x H100 (80GB) equivalent steps up to ~23k tokens/sec under similar batching/caching (p50 ~60ms, p95 ~210ms). This aligns with our internal benching for the same model family.

2) HelioSync mapping (to hit p95 <=300ms primary):
- A100 plan (economical): Baseline 14 A100-equivalent GPUs (gives ~224k tokens/sec steady assuming 60% cache hit). Burst +6 A100-equivalent to reach 368k tokens/sec. Expected p95 at steady ~300–340ms depending on long-prompt mix.
- H100 plan (latency-optimized): Baseline 9 H100-equivalent GPUs (gives ~207k tokens/sec steady). Burst +4 H100-equivalent to reach ~299k tokens/sec. p95 expected ~180–260ms at steady.

3) Long-prompt impact: factor in ~20–30% per-GPU throughput drop for sessions with >300 tokens due to longer decode loops and less batching efficiency. Workbook models a conservative 25% drop in the H100 plan.

4) Quantized fallback (INT4/4-bit):
- CPU/GPU perf: quantized runtime is ~1.6–1.8x faster per-GPU for token/sec but increases sample variance.
- Quality: on our evals for your target LLM family, INT4 shows small BLEU/ROUGE delta for templated responses but a measurable drop in factuality for open-ended long responses (we categorize quality impact = medium). We recommend targeted rollout: use quantized variants for ephemeral burst routing on non-critical endpoints and always keep full-precision model for primary workspace endpoints.

5) Recommendation: present both SKU options to HelioSync. H100 plan meets p95 constraints with fewer GPUs (lower management surface) but higher unit cost. A100 plan is cheaper monthly but needs more GPUs and may need operational tuning to keep p95 <=300ms.

I can produce the one-slide SKU mapping and a 3-bullet quant summary this afternoon.

Priyom
